title: Quanta: A Zero-Dependency Quantum Software Architecture with Apple Silicon Metal/MLX Acceleration, Continuous Hilbert Autograd, and 2026 Dual-Track Fault Tolerance
description: Quanta (v1.2.0) is a local-first, zero-dependency quantum computing and continuous Hilbert automatic differentiation framework engineered from first principles in pure Python and NumPy. Designed to eliminate binary toolchain bloat, host-to-device PCIe transfer bottlenecks, and numerical gradient drift in hybrid algorithms, Quanta introduces five foundational architectural paradigms: (1) a standalone O(2^n) tensor contraction core with thread-isolated circuit construction and native instruction sets for IBM Heron, Google Sycamore, and IonQ architectures; (2) zero-copy Apple Silicon Metal/MLX GPU acceleration eliminating PCIe overhead (peak 52.1x speedup) alongside a SIMD-vectorized Aaronson-Gottesman binary tableau simulator (>3.1M gates/s) and norm-preserving Matrix Product States (MPS); (3) continuous Hilbert space automatic differentiation via the Daleckii-Krein spectral Fréchet formula with cardinal sine kernel (IEEE 754 double precision) and Dynamical Lie Algebra (DLA) barren plateau variance bounds; (4) a 2026 Dual-Track Fault-Tolerance Engine comprising Track A (rotated surface codes with Edmonds Blossom MWPM and Google Willow 3D spacetime defect graphs) and Track B (canonical Gross [[144, 12, 12]] Bivariate Bicycle qLDPC code with native Normalized Min-Sum BP-OSD-0 decoding providing 12x physical qubit compression), 15-to-1 Bravyi-Kitaev magic state distillation, and planar lattice surgery; and (5) certified mathematical rigor with runtime conservation invariant guards enforcing spectral unitarity (< 10^-14) and CPTP trace preservation (< 10^-12) across 2,076 automated tests.
